steps.name: Workshop deck
steps.description: The workshop deck is used to guide the workshop sessions and present the key topics, processes, and ideas needed for discussion. It helps ensure the workshop stays focused and that all required areas are covered in a clear and structured way.

steps.name: Workshop Requirements Confirmation
steps.description: The workshop requirements confirmation is done after the workshop sessions to reconfirm and finalize the captured requirements. This step ensures that all discussed items are correctly understood and agreed upon, and it formally signals the start of product backlog creation.

steps.name: Product Backlog
steps.description: Creation of the product backlog based on the confirmed requirements, detailing features, user stories, and scope items to be delivered.

steps.name: Product Backlog Email Confirmation
steps.description: Formal confirmation via email to validate and approve the created product backlog.

steps.name: Dev/QA Effort Estimates
steps.description: Estimation of development and testing effort required for each backlog item to support planning and scheduling.

steps.name: Internal QA/AP Testing
steps.description: Internal testing to verify system functionality and integration before external testing.

steps.name: Endorsement Email for SIT
steps.description: Formal endorsement to confirm readiness to proceed with SIT.

steps.name: TCS QA Testing
steps.description: Execution of formal system integration testing by the QA team.

steps.name: Signed Off Email for SIT
steps.description: Formal sign-off confirming SIT completion and approval to proceed to UAT.

steps.name: Endorsement Email for UAT
steps.description: Formal endorsement confirming readiness to start UAT.

steps.name: Prepare Defect Log and other UAT Pre-artifacts
steps.description: Preparation of defect tracking and supporting materials required for UAT.

steps.name: UAT Briefing and Demonstration
steps.description: Walkthrough and demonstration of the system to guide users before testing.

steps.name: UAT Completion Report
steps.description: Documentation summarizing UAT results, findings, and final acceptance.

items.name: LHUB JIRA creation Teams group chat
Internal SharePoint Site where all FSDs uploaded

sections.title: Clarification checklist for the remote BA
items: 1. May I request the link to the reviewed FSD uploaded in the internal SharePoint site?
2. May I request the link to the Hi-Fi design for this FSD?
3. Which sections of the FSD have been fully signed off and are ready for development?
4. Who is the assigned developer for this FSD?
sections.note: Note: When the Project Manager asks for the number of tasks created, this refers to the number of FSD sections that have been reviewed and converted into Jira tickets. To determine this, count the total number of tickets listed under “Issues in Epic” on the Jira web page. This total represents the number of Jira tasks created.

sections.title: Jira ticket creation steps
items:
4. In the Create Issue screen, set the following for the Epic:
- Project: Vitae for LXP (VITAELXP)
- Issue Type: Epic
- Priority: Normal / Major
- Summary Format: [Pillar #] FSD Name
(If no Pillar is specified, use the FSD name only — do not include brackets.)
- Assignee: Assigned Developer for the FSD
Description Format:
Kindly refer to the following links:

FSD: [FSD link]
Hi-Fi Design: [Hi-Fi Design link]
5. Click Create to save the Epic.
6. Once the Epic is created, click the “+” icon next to Issues in Epic to create tasks.

7. For each Story under the Epic:
- Issue Type: Story
- Summary Format: [Pillar #] [FSD Name] FSD Section
- Assignee: Assigned Developer
- Description:
Use the same format as the Epic description.

8. If a Sub-task is required:
- Open the relevant Story from the Issues in Epic list.
- Click More (next to Assign).
- Select Create Sub-task.

9. For the Sub-task, use the following Summary Format:
- [Pillar #] [FSD Name] [FSD Section] FSD sub-section
- Assign the sub-task to the appropriate developer.
- Follow the same description format used in the Epic and Story.
